instructions.title: How to use Paste Up
instructions.intro: Paste Up prints card translations on small pieces of paper. Cut each piece out and lay it over the card's text, so the translation covers the original words and the rest of the artwork stays visible.
instructions.templateBody: A template is the HTML for one printed piece. Style it with Tailwind classes and size it in millimeters to match the text area it covers, for example <size/>. <plain/> fills in an attribute as plain text, and <html/> keeps HTML such as <tag/>.
instructions.instancesBody: Each instance fills a template with one card's attributes, written as JSON. Amount sets how many copies print. Folders group instances, and the eye icon hides an instance or a whole folder from the pages.
instructions.pagesBody: The preview shows A4 pages as they print. A row of pieces that does not fit moves to the next page. Page Class Name adds Tailwind classes to every page, for example <pageClass/> to leave space between pieces.
instructions.printBody: Open the browser's print dialog with Ctrl + P (⌘ + P on a Mac). Keep the scale at 100% and turn on background graphics so colored pieces print. Cut along each piece's border and lay it over its card's text; a card sleeve holds it in place.
instructions.saveBody: Projects save in this browser. The project menu in the header switches between them or starts a new one, and Delete in Project Setting removes the current one. Export downloads the current project as a JSON file, and Import adds one as a new project, so a translation can move between computers or translators. The buttons below add the example projects.
